:::{#thm-second-order-condition}
#### Second-order sufficient condition

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ have first and second partial derivatives
that are continuous on $\reals^p$ ([continuity](vector-calculus.qmd#def-continuous-several)).
If $\vx^*$ is a stationary point of $f$ (@def-stationary-point)
and $\matr{H}_f(\vx^*)$ is [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite),
then $\vx^*$ is a strict local minimizer of $f$ (@def-strict-local-minimizer).

:::

::: proof

$\matr{H}_f(\vx^*)$ is positive definite, and so symmetric,
so its smallest eigenvalue $\eigval$ is positive
([definiteness and eigenvalues](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-definite-eigenvalues)).
Each of the $p^2$ entries of $\matr{H}_f$ is continuous at $\vx^*$ ([continuity](vector-calculus.qmd#def-continuous-several)):
for $\tolout = \eigval / (2p)$ there is a $\tolin_{ij} > 0$ with
$\abs{\sb{\matr{H}_f(\vy)}_{ij} - \sb{\matr{H}_f(\vx^*)}_{ij}} < \eigval / (2p)$
whenever $\norm{\vy - \vx^*} < \tolin_{ij}$.
Let $\tolin$ be the smallest of these $p^2$ numbers.

Now let $0 < \norm{\vecf{h}} < \tolin$.
By @thm-taylor-mv there is a $\midpt \in (0, 1)$ for which the first step of the next display holds;
let $\vy \eqdef \vx^* + \midpt \vecf{h}$ and $\matr{E} \eqdef \matr{H}_f(\vy) - \matr{H}_f(\vx^*)$.
Since $\norm{\vy - \vx^*} = \midpt\,\norm{\vecf{h}} < \tolin$,
every entry of $\matr{E}$ has absolute value less than $\eigval / (2p)$,
so @lem-qf-entry-bound applies with $m = \eigval / (2p)$:

$$
\ba
f(\vx^* + \vecf{h}) - f(\vx^*)
&= \tp{\paren{\deriv{\vx} f(\vx^*)}} \vecf{h} + \frac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{h}}\,\matr{H}_f(\vy)\,\vecf{h}
&& \text{(@thm-taylor-mv)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{h}}\,\matr{H}_f(\vy)\,\vecf{h}
&& \text{(} \vx^* \text{ is stationary)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{h}}\,\matr{H}_f(\vx^*)\,\vecf{h} + \frac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{h}}\,\matr{E}\,\vecf{h}
&& \text{(} \matr{H}_f(\vy) = \matr{H}_f(\vx^*) + \matr{E} \text{; distribute)}
\\
&\ge \frac{1}{2}\,\eigval\,\norm{\vecf{h}}^2 + \frac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{h}}\,\matr{E}\,\vecf{h}
&& \text{(@lem-qf-eigen-bound)}
\\
&\ge \frac{1}{2}\,\eigval\,\norm{\vecf{h}}^2 - \frac{1}{2}\,\abs{\tp{\vecf{h}}\,\matr{E}\,\vecf{h}}
&& \text{(a number is at least minus its absolute value)}
\\
&\ge \frac{1}{2}\,\eigval\,\norm{\vecf{h}}^2 - \frac{1}{2}\,p\,\frac{\eigval}{2p}\,\norm{\vecf{h}}^2
&& \text{(@lem-qf-entry-bound, } m = \eigval / (2p) \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{\eigval}{4}\,\norm{\vecf{h}}^2
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\
&> 0.
&& \text{(} \eigval > 0 \text{ and } \vecf{h} \ne \vzero \text{)}
\ea
$$

So $f(\vx^*) < f(\vx)$ whenever $0 < \norm{\vx - \vx^*} < \tolin$ (take $\vecf{h} = \vx - \vx^*$).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-second-order-condition}
#### Classifying stationary points

- $f(\vx) = x_1^2 + x_2^2 - 2 x_1$ has the stationary point $\tp{(1, 0)}$ (@exm-stationary-point),
  and its Hessian is $\matr{H}_f(\vx) = \sbmat{ 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 } = 2 \matr{I}_2$,
  which is positive definite, so $\tp{(1, 0)}$ is a strict local minimizer.
- $f(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^2$ has the stationary point $\vzero$
  and Hessian $\sbmat{ 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 }$, which is not positive definite
  ($\tp{(0, 1)}$ gives $-2$),
  and indeed $\vzero$ is not a local minimizer (@exm-first-order-condition).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-second-order-inconclusive}
#### The condition is sufficient, not necessary

$f(\vx) = x_1^2 + x_2^4$ and $g(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^4$
both have gradient $\vzero$ at $\vzero$
and the same Hessian there, $\sbmat{ 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 }$,
since $\deriv{x_2} \paren{\deriv{x_2} (\pm x_2^4)} = \pm 12 x_2^2 = 0$ at $x_2 = 0$.
That Hessian is not positive definite ($\tp{(0, 1)}$ gives $0$),
so @thm-second-order-condition says nothing about either function.
In fact $\vzero$ is a strict local minimizer of $f$,
since $f(\vx) > 0 = f(\vzero)$ for $\vx \ne \vzero$,
but not a local minimizer of $g$, since $g(0, t) = -t^4 < 0 = g(\vzero)$ for $t \ne 0$.

:::
